/-!
# Erdős Problem 997

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/997](https://www.erdosproblems.com/997)
- [APSSV26] B. Alexeev, M. Putterman, M. Sawhney, M. Sellke, and G. Valiant,
  [Short proofs in combinatorics and number theory](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.29961).
  arXiv:2603.29961 (2026).
- [CLLW24] J. Champagne, T. Le, Y.-R. Liu, and T. D. Wooley, Well-distribution modulo one and the
  primes. arXiv:2406.19491 (2024).
- [Er64b] Erdős, P., Problems and results on diophantine approximations. Compositio Math. (1964),
  52-65.
- [Er85e] Erdős, P., Some problems and results in number theory. Number theory and combinatorics.
  Japan 1984 (Tokyo, Okayama and Kyoto, 1984) (1985), 65-87.
- [Hl55] Hlawka, Edmund, Zur formalen {T}heorie der {G}leichverteilung in kompakten {G}ruppen. Rend.
  Circ. Mat. Palermo (2) (1955), 33--47.
- [Mo26] P. Monticone, [Lean formalisation of Erdős problem 997](https://live.lean-lang.org/#project=mathlib-v4.28.0&url=https://gist.githubusercontent.com/pitmonticone/016f2ed66b4cd1c4c4b9998095170e60/raw/b7dfc05c525ae385b5835f89f1ada721443e4305/Erdos997.lean) (2026)
-/

open Set

namespace Erdos997

/--
Call $x_1,x_2,\ldots \in (0,1)$ well-distributed if, for every $\epsilon>0$, if $k$ is
sufficiently large then, for all $n>0$ and intervals $I\subseteq [0,1]$,
$\lvert \# \{ n < m\leq n+k : x_m\in I\} - \lvert I\rvert k\rvert < \epsilon k.$

The notion of a well-distributed sequence was introduced by Hlawka and Petersen [Hl55].
-/
def IsWellDistributed (x : ℕ → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ ε > 0, ∀ᶠ k in Filter.atTop, ∀ n : ℕ,
  ∀ a b, 0 ≤ a → a ≤ b → b ≤ 1 →
    letI I := Ico a b
    let count := (Finset.Ioc n (n + k)).filter (fun m ↦ x m ∈ I)
    abs ((count.card : ℝ) - (b - a) * k) < ε * k

/--
Is it true that, for every $\alpha$, the sequence $\{ \alpha p_n\}$ is not well-distributed,
if $p_n$ is the sequence of primes?

The answer is yes, by [APSSV26, Section 4]; a Lean formalisation is available in [Mo26].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://live.lean-lang.org/#project=mathlib-v4.28.0&url=https://gist.githubusercontent.com/pitmonticone/016f2ed66b4cd1c4c4b9998095170e60/raw/b7dfc05c525ae385b5835f89f1ada721443e4305/Erdos997.lean"]
theorem erdos_997 :
    answer(True) ↔
      ∀ α : ℝ, ¬ IsWellDistributed (fun n ↦ Int.fract (α * (n.nth Nat.Prime))) := by
  sorry

/--
Erdős proved that, if $n_k$ is a lacunary sequence, then the sequence $\{ \alpha n_k\}$ is not
well-distributed for almost all $\alpha$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_997.variants.lacunary (n : ℕ → ℕ) (h : IsLacunary n) :
    ∀ᵐ α, ¬ IsWellDistributed (fun k ↦ Int.fract (α * (n k : ℝ))) := by
  sorry

/--
He also claimed in [Er64b] to have proved that there exists an irrational $\alpha$ for which
$\{\alpha p_n\}$ is not well-distributed. He later retracted this claim in [Er85e], saying "The
theorem is no doubt correct and perhaps will not be difficult to prove but I never was able to
reconstruct my 'proof' which perhaps never existed."

The existence of such an $\alpha$ was established by Champagne, Le, Liu, and Wooley [CLLW24].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_997.variants.irrational :
    ∃ α : ℝ, Irrational α ∧
      ¬ IsWellDistributed (fun n ↦ Int.fract (α * (n.nth Nat.Prime))) := by
  sorry

end Erdos997

reformulations.difference: Lean uses half-open intervals Ico a b and permits starting index n = 0, whereas APSSV26 Section 4 uses closed intervals [a,b] and n ≥ 1.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: These choices are equivalent on every sequence used in this file, since fractional parts lie in [0,1). Enlarging or shrinking interval endpoints with epsilon slack transfers the discrepancy condition between half-open and closed intervals. A fixed shift by d changes any block count by at most d, hence its normalized discrepancy by at most d/k; permitting the additional initial starting index therefore does not change well-distribution. The epsilon/eventually formulation is the source's vanishing uniform discrepancy condition. In /workspace/review/equivalences.lean, halfopen_iff_positive_closed proves the endpoint/start-index equivalence after expanding the limit condition, and wellDistributed_iff_shift proves shift invariance. Their axiom lists contain only the standard Lean axioms.

reformulations.difference: IsLacunary requires c * n k < n (k+1) only eventually, allowing an arbitrary initial segment, whereas Er64b states the result for a positive sequence with n_(k+1)/n_k > λ > 1 throughout.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The house predicate guarantees a tail consisting entirely of positive terms with the required multiplicative gaps. On positive terms, the product and ratio inequalities are equivalent. Apply the source theorem to that tail and transfer non-well-distribution back using shift invariance, pointwise in alpha; the same exceptional null set works. Conversely, a globally positive lacunary sequence satisfies IsLacunary. The full quantified equivalence between the eventual-gap and positive-global-gap claims is proved as lacunary_claim_iff in /workspace/review/equivalences.lean, without using the file's sorry theorems.

reformulations.difference: CLLW24 defines well-distribution by convergence for each fixed interval, uniformly in the starting index. The shared Lean definition additionally makes the sufficiently-large block-length threshold uniform over all intervals.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The conditions are equivalent. For a given epsilon, choose a finite grid in [0,1] of mesh less than epsilon/8. Apply the fixed-interval condition to the finitely many grid intervals with error epsilon/2, and take the largest threshold. Sandwich each arbitrary interval between grid intervals; their lengths differ from its length by at most twice the mesh. If an inner interval is empty, use the zero lower bound instead. This gives the uniform epsilon discrepancy estimate for every interval and starting index. The converse is immediate. Thus the stronger-looking quantifier order does not change CLLW24's existence statement.

review.notes: All four mathematical declarations were checked; no mathematical misformalizations were found. Scratch tests confirmed the Lebesgue-measure interpretation of ∀ᵐ, valid zero-indexed prime enumeration, block cardinality k, empty-interval behavior, satisfiability of IsLacunary via 2^k, and failure of well-distribution for the zero sequence. Boundary tests and equivalence proofs compile successfully. The exact external proof also compiles, with the custom-axiom dependency reported above. Direct access to erdosproblems.com/997 returned a Cloudflare 403 despite descriptive User-Agent headers; the other cited primary sources independently establish the statements and solved statuses. Hlawka's full text was unavailable, but the needed definition is explicit in Er64b, APSSV26, and CLLW24. The reviewed file's hash matches the supplied commit; no repository files were edited.
